overall_summary: Analysis of recent observations shows that space-based 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary facts (such as Venus's day/year anomaly, liquid diamond planets, and extreme dark planets) heavily outperform standard biology or generic psychology facts. Videos published in late September and October 2026 (e.g., A9Qa-RmuOr0, IYuce8vaU3Y, 8KEl0_pJ_68) demonstrate significantly higher views-per-day velocity and stronger engagement (likes-per-view) compared to older September content, proving that speculative space geography and counterintuitive physics hooks are driving current algorithmic traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generated over 900-1000+ views rapidly with high like conversion.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical space immersion scenarios featuring extreme cosmic materials.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) achieved near 1,000 views with strong engagement right after publication.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on bizarre planetary physics and time anomalies that defy normal human intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) stalled out at 5 to 10 views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize internal biological/psychological micro-facts in favor of external cosmic or geographical phenomena.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic single-fact animal shorts without a narrative stakes element (e.g., F1kXwuXuNgo) underperformed relative to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content towards cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic trivia.
